title: Sanctuary Typology Blueprint & Chronological Plan of Salvation
description: Deterministic knowledge graph of the Hebrew sanctuary/tabernacle, its compartments, furniture, sacrificial services, Christological fulfillment, and chronological plan of salvation per Fundamental Belief #24 and ADR-025.

compartments.name: The Courtyard
compartments.significance: The realm of the earth where the sacrificial Lamb was slain (Calvary). Represents justification by faith and the sphere of public sacrifice.
compartments.materials: Hangings of fine twined linen, pillars of brass, silver fillets and hooks

compartments.name: The Holy Place
compartments.significance: The first apartment of the tabernacle, representing Christ's daily, continual intercessory ministry as High Priest in the Heavenly Sanctuary between His ascension and 1844. Represents sanctification, illumination, nourishment, and prayer.
compartments.materials: Boards of acacia wood overlaid with pure gold, curtains of fine linen embroidered with cherubim in blue, purple, and scarlet

compartments.name: The Most Holy Place
compartments.significance: The second apartment (Holy of Holies), a perfect cube housing the Ark of the Covenant and Shekinah Glory. Entered by the High Priest only on Yom Kippur (Day of Atonement) for the cleansing of the sanctuary, typifying Christ's final phase of ministry beginning in 1844: the investigative judgment and vindication of God's character.
compartments.materials: Inner veil of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine twined linen with cherubim; walls of gold; solid gold Mercy Seat
compartments.spiritual_reality: Vindication / Cleansing of the Sanctuary / Final Judgment

stations.name: Altar of Burnt Offering
stations.materials: Acacia wood overlaid with brass (bronze), hollow with boards, brass grating, four horns on corners
stations.position: Courtyard, before the entrance of the Tabernacle
stations.theological_meaning: The Cross of Christ and the complete substitutionary atonement. Represents justification by faith: the innocent dying for the guilty, reconciling sinners to God.
stations.priestly_service: Daily morning and evening continual burnt offering (Tamid); individual sin offerings where blood was applied to the horns and poured out at the base; perpetual sacred fire never to go out.
stations.sda_consensus: The courtyard represents this earth, where Christ offered His life as the spotless Lamb of God. The brazen altar points exclusively to Calvary: an all-sufficient, unrepeatable sacrifice providing justification to all who believe.

stations.name: The Laver
stations.materials: Brass (bronze), made from the polished bronze mirrors donated by the women who ministered at the tabernacle door
stations.position: Courtyard, between the Altar of Burnt Offering and the door of the Tabernacle
stations.theological_meaning: Cleansing, regeneration, and the washing of water by the Word. Prefigures Christian baptism and the daily sanctifying purification of the Holy Spirit.
stations.priestly_service: Priests washed their hands and feet before entering the Holy Place or approaching the altar to minister, under penalty of death, demonstrating that unholiness cannot abide in God's presence.
stations.sda_consensus: Just as the altar represents justification, the laver represents regeneration and washing from defilement. Before engaging in spiritual ministry, the believer must experience the renewing of the Holy Spirit.

stations.name: The Golden Lampstand
stations.materials: One solid talent of pure beaten gold; central shaft with six branches, knops, flowers, and seven almond-shaped oil lamps
stations.position: Holy Place, south side (left upon entering)
stations.theological_meaning: Christ the Light of the World, the sevenfold fullness of the Holy Spirit, and the Church commissioned to shine in spiritual darkness through divine oil.
stations.priestly_service: Daily dressed every morning and filled every evening with pure beaten olive oil, burning continually without ceasing to illuminate the holy vessels.
stations.sda_consensus: The golden lampstand with its continual flame symbolizes the Holy Spirit and Christ walking among the seven candlesticks of His church (Rev 1:13). Not by might nor by power, but by My Spirit, saith the Lord (Zech 4:6).

stations.name: Table of Shewbread
stations.materials: Acacia wood overlaid with pure gold, bordered with a golden crown and border of a handbreadth; golden dishes, spoons, covers, and bowls
stations.position: Holy Place, north side (right upon entering)
stations.theological_meaning: Christ the Bread of Life, the life-giving Word of God, covenant communion, and God's perpetual provision for every tribe of His people.
stations.spiritual_reality: Nourishment / The Living Word / Covenant Fellowship
stations.priestly_service: Twelve loaves of unleavened bread baked with fine flour, placed in two stacks of six with pure frankincense upon each row, replaced every Sabbath day and eaten by the consecrated priests.
stations.sda_consensus: The bread of the Presence represents both the Living Word (Christ) and the written Word of God. As the twelve loaves stood continually before God, so believers are fed on the Sabbath and sustained in spiritual life by feeding on Christ.

stations.name: Altar of Incense
stations.materials: Acacia wood overlaid with pure gold, golden crown, four golden horns, staves overlaid with gold
stations.position: Holy Place, west end, immediately before the veil separating the Holy from the Most Holy Place
stations.theological_meaning: Christ's intercessory righteousness and merits mingled with the prayers of the saints. Teaches that human prayers are accepted by the Father only through the fragrance of Christ's merits.
stations.priestly_service: Perpetual sweet incense burned morning and evening when the lamps were trimmed; fire taken only from the brazen altar; blood placed on its horns on the Day of Atonement and during the sin offering.
stations.sda_consensus: The smoke of the incense ascending before the veil represents Christ's spotless righteousness which alone makes our prayers acceptable before God. He ever liveth to make intercession for them (Heb 7:25).

stations.name: Ark of the Covenant
stations.common_name: Ark of the Testimony & Mercy Seat
stations.materials: Acacia chest overlaid inside and out with pure gold; solid gold Mercy Seat (Kapporet) with two golden Cherubim gazing downward toward the Law with wings overshadowing; golden crown around rim
stations.position: Most Holy Place, center, beneath the Shekinah Glory
stations.theological_meaning: The throne room of the Sovereign God, where mercy and truth meet together, righteousness and peace kiss each other (Ps 85:10). The Ten Commandments within represent God's eternal moral law as the standard of judgment; the Mercy Seat above demonstrates that redemption covers law-transgression.
stations.spiritual_reality: Throne of God / Moral Law / Propitiation / Final Judgment
stations.priestly_service: Entered exclusively by the High Priest once a year on Yom Kippur (Leviticus 16) with incense and sacrificial blood, sprinkled seven times upon and before the Mercy Seat to cleanse the sanctuary from all Israel's transgressions.
stations.sda_consensus: The Ark contains the unchanging Law of God, including the fourth commandment Sabbath. In the heavenly sanctuary, Christ entered the Most Holy Place in 1844 to commence the investigative judgment, vindicating God's character and blotting out the sins of the faithful before His return (Dan 7:9-14, 8:14, Rev 11:19).

services.name: The Daily Service (Tamid / Continual)
services.frequency: Daily, morning and evening, throughout the year
services.focus: Transfer of sin, forgiveness, continual justification, maintenance of communion
services.process: The sinner brought an unblemished animal, laid hands on its head confessing sin (symbolically transferring guilt), and slew the victim. The priest caught the blood and either sprinkled it before the veil of the Holy Place or ate the flesh in the holy place, thus transferring the record of sin into the sanctuary (Lev 4, Lev 6:25-26).
services.christological_antitype: Christ's continual mediation as our heavenly High Priest, applying the benefits of His once-for-all sacrifice at Calvary to every repentant sinner who comes to God by Him (Heb 7:25).

services.name: The Yearly Service (Yom Kippur / Day of Atonement)
services.frequency: Tenth day of the seventh month (Tishri 10)
services.participants: High Priest alone, entire nation afflicting their souls
services.focus: Cleansing of the sanctuary, blotting out of confessed sins, final eradication of sin, vindication of God
services.process: Two goats were chosen: the Lord's goat and the scapegoat (Azazel). The Lord's goat was slain and its blood carried by the High Priest inside the veil to cleanse the Mercy Seat and sanctuary from all accumulated sins. Having made an end of cleansing the holy place, the High Priest laid his hands on the scapegoat, confessed over it all the iniquities of Israel, and sent it away into the wilderness bearing the ultimate guilt.
services.christological_antitype: The investigative judgment and cleansing of the heavenly sanctuary begun in 1844 at the end of the 2300 prophetic days (Dan 8:14, Heb 9:23-28). Christ vindicates the penitent, blots out their sins from the books of heaven, and places final responsibility for evil upon Satan, the originator of sin.

plan_of_salvation.title: The Earthly Sacrifice: Justification at the Cross
plan_of_salvation.historical_event: The First Advent: Incarnation, sinless life, death of Christ at Calvary, resurrection, and ascension.
plan_of_salvation.theological_significance: The complete, all-sufficient sacrifice offered once for all. Justification by faith imputed to the believer; the legal basis for all subsequent mediation.

plan_of_salvation.title: Heavenly Inauguration & Continual Intercession
plan_of_salvation.historical_event: Christ inaugurated as High Priest at Pentecost (Acts 2), ministering His blood before the Father in the first apartment of the heavenly sanctuary.
plan_of_salvation.theological_significance: Sanctification and continuous intercession. Christ mediates the prayers of the saints, dispenses the Holy Spirit, feeds His church through the Word, and forgives daily sins.

plan_of_salvation.title: The Cleansing of the Sanctuary & Investigative Judgment
plan_of_salvation.historical_event: Termination of the 2300 prophetic days (Dan 8:14). The Ancient of Days sits in judgment (Dan 7:9-10), and Christ enters the Most Holy Place to cleanse the sanctuary.
plan_of_salvation.theological_significance: The final phase of Christ's atoning ministry: examining the records of all who have professed faith, vindicating God's righteous character before the universe, and permanently blotting out sins prior to the Second Coming.

plan_of_salvation.title: Final Disposition of Sin & The Earth Made New
plan_of_salvation.historical_event: Close of probation, Christ returns as King of kings, millennium in heaven, final eradication of Satan and sin, New Jerusalem descends upon Earth Made New.
plan_of_salvation.theological_significance: Glorification and eternal security. The universe is cleansed of sin; God tabernacles forever with redeemed humanity in perfect righteousness.
